pages.title: A obra e a situação

work.title: The Italian Job
work.note: The Italian Job, de 1969, dirigido por Peter Collinson, mostra Charlie Croker, vivido por Michael Caine, planejando roubar ouro em Turim. A obra conversa com o foco porque a aula transforma esse contexto em falar de prova: I took the test. I passed! He failed the test, so he will retake it. What was your mark?. A referência mostra o desafio de dirigir bem: pass the test.

facts.label: Passado e planos
facts.sub: Use o passado simples para ontem: We ate pizza. Use going to para planos: I’m going to play it this weekend.

facts.label: Passado simples
facts.sub: Para falar de ontem, use o passado simples: My friends came at six. We ate pizza. Mom made a big cake. Come, eat e make são irregulares: came, ate, made.

facts.label: Did
facts.sub: Para perguntar sobre o passado, use did + verbo base: Did you get presents? What did you eat? Não use got ou ate depois de did. A resposta é Yes, I did.

pages.title: A small house · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Sunday morning in a small house in Halifax. Colorful balloons are still on the ceiling. Leo sits on the sofa with a cup of juice. His friend Hugo comes in. There is a lot of paper on the floor. Hugo missed the party and wants to hear about it.
“Hi, Leo! How was your birthday party yesterday?” says Hugo. “It was great! My friends came at six.” says Leo. “What did you eat?” says Hugo.
